headline: BNP leaders take Rajshahi Medical University VC to campus from home
summary: Two more people were arrested as authorities opened the locked VC's office to collect evidence following allegations of forced resignation.
details: BNP and affiliate organization leaders took Rajshahi Medical University (RMU) Vice-Chancellor Professor Jawadul Haque from his residence to the university's temporary campus on Thursday.
The VC had previously alleged that he was forced to sign a document under threat of physical assault on Tuesday, after which he was removed from his office.
Following the incident, reports emerged that the VC's mobile phone and laptop were taken, and the CPU and hard disk of the CCTV cameras were removed from the premises.
On Thursday morning, an executive magistrate opened the locked VC's office, allowing investigating officers to collect evidence from the room.
Two more individuals, Ali Akbar Hossain and Delwar Hossain, have been arrested in connection with the case filed at Rajpara Police Station.
Rajshahi Metropolitan Police (RMP) stated that several other suspects have been identified through video and photo analysis and will be arrested soon.
caption:
BNP leaders took the RMU Vice-Chancellor from his home to campus after he was allegedly forced to sign a resignation letter.

BNP and affiliate organization leaders took Rajshahi Medical University (RMU) Vice-Chancellor Professor Jawadul Haque from his residence to the university's temporary campus on Thursday.

The VC had previously alleged that he was forced to sign a document under threat of physical assault on Tuesday, after which he was removed from his office.

Following the incident, reports emerged that the VC's mobile phone and laptop were taken, and the CPU and hard disk of the CCTV cameras were removed from the premises.

On Thursday morning, an executive magistrate opened the locked VC's office, allowing investigating officers to collect evidence from the room.

Two more individuals, Ali Akbar Hossain and Delwar Hossain, have been arrested in connection with the case filed at Rajpara Police Station.

Rajshahi Metropolitan Police (RMP) stated that several other suspects have been identified through video and photo analysis and will be arrested soon.

headline: Government to set up separate heart disease centers across Bangladesh
summary: State Minister for Health Dr. M.A. Muhit announced the plan to make cardiac care accessible to all, focusing on specialized equipment and trained experts.
details: The Bangladesh government is planning to establish separate heart disease treatment centers across the country to ensure that healthcare services are within reach of all citizens.
State Minister for Health Dr. M.A. Muhit announced this during a World Heart Day event in the capital on Thursday, stating that initiatives are being taken based on financial capacity.
The Minister emphasized that the plan involves more than just installing modern equipment; there is a critical need to increase the number of trained cardiac specialists to staff these centers.
Dr. Muhit identified heart disease as one of the leading causes of death in Bangladesh and urged the public to walk regularly as a preventive measure.
He also called for the appointment of trained counselors in hospitals to support patients and the creation of a network of cardiac ambulances to ensure faster emergency response.
The initiative aims to improve the overall quality of cardiac care and reduce the mortality rate associated with heart-related illnesses nationwide.
caption:
Heart disease is one of the leading causes of death in Bangladesh. To combat this, the government is planning to set up separate cardiac centers nationwide.

The Bangladesh government is planning to establish separate heart disease treatment centers across the country to ensure that healthcare services are within reach of all citizens.

State Minister for Health Dr. M.A. Muhit announced this during a World Heart Day event in the capital on Thursday, stating that initiatives are being taken based on financial capacity.

The Minister emphasized that the plan involves more than just installing modern equipment; there is a critical need to increase the number of trained cardiac specialists to staff these centers.

Dr. Muhit identified heart disease as one of the leading causes of death in Bangladesh and urged the public to walk regularly as a preventive measure.

He also called for the appointment of trained counselors in hospitals to support patients and the creation of a network of cardiac ambulances to ensure faster emergency response.

The initiative aims to improve the overall quality of cardiac care and reduce the mortality rate associated with heart-related illnesses nationwide.
